weeks.title: Sound Design: Music Selection, Mood and Audio Balance

lessons.title: Welcome — Sound Design
lessons.content:
Welcome to a new week of your video editing journey!

In today's lesson, we will explore sound design and how sound influences the way viewers experience a video.

Sound is more than something that plays in the background. It helps communicate emotions, establish atmosphere, create excitement, and make visual storytelling more powerful.

You will learn how to select suitable music, understand the mood different sounds create, identify appropriate beats, and synchronise music with your visuals.

We will also look at how to balance background music with spoken dialogue to achieve a clean and professional audio experience.

lessons.title: 1 — Why Sound Matters
lessons.content:
Understand the important role sound plays in video editing.

You will learn how music, voice, and other audio elements influence emotions, strengthen storytelling, and shape the viewer's overall experience.

lessons.title: 2 — Music Selection and Understanding Mood
lessons.content:
Learn how to choose music that matches the purpose, message, and atmosphere of your video.

You will explore how different sounds and musical styles create different moods, such as excitement, suspense, happiness, sadness, and inspiration.

lessons.title: 3 — Beat Selection
lessons.content:
Discover how to identify suitable beats and musical sections for your edits.

You will learn why choosing music with the right rhythm and energy can make your video more engaging and help your visuals feel connected.

lessons.title: 4 — Music Timing
lessons.content:
Learn how to position music within your timeline and synchronise important visual moments with the rhythm of your chosen track.

You will understand how to time music entrances, transitions, cuts, and endings to create a smoother editing experience.

lessons.title: 5 — Voice and Music Balance
lessons.content:
Understand how to balance background music with spoken dialogue.

You will learn how to adjust audio levels so that music supports the video without overpowering the speaker, ensuring that your audience can hear and understand the message clearly.

lessons.title: Your Learning Goal
lessons.content:
By the end of this lesson, you should understand why sound matters in video editing, how to select music that matches a video's mood, how to identify suitable beats, how to synchronise music with visuals, and how to balance background music with voice recordings.

Remember: sound helps your audience feel what your visuals are communicating. The right music, at the right moment and volume, can transform an ordinary video into a more engaging and memorable experience.

lessons.title: Tuesday — Sound Effects and Audio Layering
lessons.content:
Welcome back to another practical lesson in your video editing journey!

In today's lesson, we will explore sound effects (SFX) and how they can make your videos more engaging, expressive, and professional. Sound effects help bring visual actions to life, emphasise important moments, create atmosphere, and make edits feel more impactful.

You will learn about different types of sound effects, how to layer them, and how to match them with movements and actions in your videos. The goal is to understand how to use sound intentionally rather than simply adding effects wherever they seem appropriate.

lessons.title: 1 — Understanding Sound Effects
lessons.content:
Learn what sound effects are and the role they play in video editing.

You will discover how different sounds can support visual storytelling, create atmosphere, communicate actions, and make specific moments more noticeable.

lessons.title: 2 — Types of Sound Effects
lessons.content:
Explore different sound effects commonly used in video editing, including:

- Whooshes: Used to accompany fast movements, transitions, swipes, and objects moving across the screen.
- Impacts: Used to emphasise dramatic moments, strong movements, transitions, or important visual reveals.
- Risers: Sounds that gradually build intensity to create anticipation before an important moment.
- Clicks: Small, precise sounds often used for interface interactions, selections, and subtle visual actions.
- Pops: Short, playful sounds used to highlight text, objects, animations, and other visual elements.
- Environmental Sounds: Sounds that recreate or support real-world surroundings, such as rain, traffic, footsteps, wind, crowds, and nature.

lessons.title: 3 — Layering Sounds
lessons.content:
Learn how to combine multiple sound effects with background music and voice recordings to create a richer audio experience.

You will understand how to arrange different sounds so that they complement one another without making the audio overwhelming or cluttered.

lessons.title: 4 — Matching Sound Effects to Movement
lessons.content:
Discover how to synchronise sound effects with actions and movements on screen.

For example, a whoosh can accompany a fast transition, an impact can match an object landing, and a click can match a button appearing or being pressed.

You will learn why accurate timing matters and how synchronising sound with movement makes edits feel more natural and satisfying.

lessons.title: 5 — Creating Emphasis Through Sound
lessons.content:
Understand how sound effects can draw attention to important moments, highlight information, strengthen transitions, and create emotional impact.

You will learn how to use sound strategically to guide the viewer's attention and make key moments more memorable.

lessons.title: Your Learning Goal
lessons.content:
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to identify and use different types of sound effects, layer sounds effectively, synchronise SFX with on-screen movements, and use audio to create emphasis and strengthen your video edits.

Remember: great sound design is not about using as many sound effects as possible; it is about choosing the right sound, at the right moment, for the right purpose.
